responsibility: This file implements GCC’s middle-end handling of built-in functions at expansion time. It owns creation-time tables and many of the target-independent expansion and fallback routines that recognize builtins, fold simple constant cases, describe builtin side effects through fnspec metadata, and lower important builtins such as memory/string functions, varargs helpers, alloca, prefetch, classification/math builtins, and assorted target-sensitive intrinsics into RTL or libcalls, while also providing diagnostics and object-size/access checking paths used when builtin semantics depend on argument validity or optimization knowledge.
same_name_distinction: Implementation file in the `builtins` group: unlike `gcc/builtins.def`, which declaratively enumerates builtin IDs/names/types/attributes, and `gcc/builtins.h`, which exposes the callable API and target_builtins state, this file contains the executable expansion, folding, checking, and fnspec logic that lowers builtin calls during RTL generation.
